mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized) and low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) signals an accommodative monetary policy amid rising prices, which typically triggers equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST > 600 thousand units), rising home construction activity signals strong consumer confidence and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where HOUST > 600 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO > 95.0) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO > 95.0 (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 3.0%, it signals a loss of monetary policy control that increases real interest rates and equity risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS > 100k monthly) and weak retail sales (RSAFS < 340,000 million) indicates a disconnect between job gains and consumer spending, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS > 100k and RSAFS < 340,000) fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.0%), the Federal Reserve typically implements aggressive monetary easing, which boosts equity valuations and generates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE > 6.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).
